item.title: Values
item.description:
Templates have 6 primitive values Identifiers Strings numbers function calls Arrays Maps These are used to represent values in luauStrings are created using 2 " surrounding its contents| ID : "Testing123" Numbers are directly written just like luau| DisplayDistance : 123 Identifiers are created when defining a cinnamon object using the ID property<Container> | ID : "Test123" </Container> in this example a new identifier is created called Test123 which represents a UIContainer. Identifiers can then be later referenced further down the template.Identifiers cannot be referenced before they're definedinvalid as its referenced before it exists<Container> | ID : "Test456" | Parent : Test123 </Container> <Container> | ID : "Test123" </Container> function calls are formatted as <functionName>(Arguments)there are currently 6 functions available <ref>(string) - Gets a value from reference table <rad>(number) - Converts number (in degrees) to radians <prop>(identifier) - Gets property of cinnamon object <vec3>([number]) - creates a vector3 <vec2>([number]) - creates a vector2 <cframe>([number] | [vec3]) - creates a cframe <angles>([number]) - creates a cframe using CFrame.Angles Example:<container> | ID : "container_2" | Parent : container_1 | Origin : <cframe>([0,0,0]) | UI : <ref>("UI") </container> Arrays are formatted as [itemA,ItemB,ItemC] These represent tables used as arrays in luauMaps are created using curly brackets{ ["Index"] : Value, ["Index2"] : Value2, } These represent tables in luauPrevious Headers
Next Containers & elements

item.title: Headers
item.description:
Header Files are meta data that hold information like the version of cinnamon. Primarily meant to be used for editors reading the file.header example:<Header> | version : "0.2" </Header> headers dont construct anything themselves but must be included in your file to be valid, as files without Headers will not compile.Previous Getting started
Next Values

item.title: Animation
Layouts
item.description:
Template files precompute layouts on compilation. So they aren't dynamically created.Example of a layout<layout> | ID : "layout_0" | Callback : <ref>("Radial") | Elements : [node_1] | Props : { ["Distance"] : 10, ["Padding"] : <rad>(5), ["Origin"] : <prop>(node_0,"Origin"), ["StartAngle"] : 0, ["Axis"] : <vec3>([0,1,0]) } </layout> Layouts computes its cframe values using the callback you provide for it. The callback being a function in your reference table.callbacks must include 2 arguments elements - a table of elements Props - a table/value thats inputted into your callback Heres how it would be usedlocal Source = require(script.["Template.cinm"]) local Reference = { Radial = Cinnamon.Layout.Radial } local Import = Cinnamon.Compile(Source,Reference) Cinnamon.Layout.ApplyLayout(Import["Container"].Elements,Import["layout_0"]) Previous Containers & Elements
Next Animation

item.title: Containers_&_elements
Getting_started
item.description: Template files are structured markup files how cinnamon objects are structured and assembled.Instead of creating large constructor methods, you define your object structure using cinnamon's template file format. These templates can be compiled at run time to create active cinnamon objects.template files use the extension .cinm to differentiate themselves from normal module scriptsCinnamon template file source:<header> | version : "0.2" </header> <container> | ID : "node_0" | Origin : <cframe>([ 0, 10, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1 ]) | UI : <ref>("UI") <element> | UI : <ref>("Frame") | ID : "node_1" | Offset : <cframe>([0, 0, 0]) | Face : "Front" | Resolution : <vec2>([200,200]) </element> </container> <animation> | ID : "spring_0" | Type : "Spring" | Instance : node_1 | Props : { ["Goal"] : <cframe>([<vec3>([0,0,0]),<vec3>([1,0,0])]), ["Property"] : "Offset", ["Damping"] : 0.5, ["Frequency"] : 1, ["Response"] : -1, ["Time"] : 1 } </animation> Require the file your compiling local Template = require(script["Template.cinm"]) make the reference table (must match the strings passed into <ref>() calls) local ScreenGui = PlayerGui:WaitForChild("ScreenGui") local Frame = ScreenGui.Frame local template = require(script["Template.cinm"]) local Reference = { UI = ScreenGui, Frame = Frame, Radial = Cinnamon.Layout.Radial, Frame2 = ScreenGui.Frame2 } Use Cinnamon.Compile to generate from file local Import = Cinnamon.Compile(template,Reference) local Container = Import["node_0"] local Spring : Cinnamon.Spring<CFrame> = Import["spring_0"] Maintability - this keeps runtime logic seperate from construction Reusability - you can create reusable components without worrying about runtime logic Cleaner architecture - Instead of using large construction functions, this keeps construction declarative and readable Editor Integration - this allows for external tools or visual editors to generate .cinm files, allowing for UI design without scripting knowledge Next Headers

item.title: Element
item.description: Stores and displays your UI in space.Properties:Enabled : Boolean Determines if your UI is being displayed or not Debug : Boolean Adds/Removes the element from the Debug visualizer Offset: CFrame Determines position and rotation relative to its parent container Resolution: Vector2 Determines the size of your UI in pixels Members:UI : GuiObject The UI thats being displayed Parent2D : GuiObject | ScreenGui The UI's parent UI Instance : Part The physical Part that holds your UI Container: UIContainer | ScreenContainer The parent Container of the element Type : string Used for typechecking

item.title: Animatables
Animation
Cinnamon
Intro
item.description: Cinnamon is a open source 3d UI framework to give developers a versatile and richer UI framework that goes beyond other 3d ui libraries.The aim of this framework is to give developers more creative control when making user interfaces in 3d, with support for things like animations, layouts, and reusable components.For more information check out the API Declarative hierarchy Cinnamon introduces Elements, which represents the individual UIs that are being displayed. Each Element is stored in a Container. -- this creates a container local Container = Cinnamon.NewContainer(ScreenGui,CFrame.new(0,2,0)) -- this creates a element for a UI frame local Element = Container:Element({ UI = ScreenGui.Frame, Offset = CFrame.new(5,0,5), Resolution = Vector2.new(100,100), }) containers can be nested inside other containers, creating a tree like hierarchy.-- this acts like a reusable component local CreateExample = function(Container,Origin) local InnerContainer = Container:NewContainer(Container.UI,Origin) InnerContainer:Element({ UI = ScreenGui.TextButton, Offset = CFrame.new(0,0,5), Resolution = Vector2.new(200,100) }) return InnerContainer end) local Container = Cinnamon.NewContainer(ScreenGui,CFrame.new(0,2,0)) local Example = CreateExample(Container,CFrame.new(0,5,0)) Layouts Cinnamon grants developers a easy way to layout their components in space, Allowing for quicker workflows and quick testing for ideas. local Container = Cinnamon.NewContainer(ScreenGui,CFrame.new(0,2,0)) for _,v in ScreenGui:GetChildren() do Container:Element({ UI = v, Resolution = Vector2.new(200,100) }) end local Layout = Cinnamon.Layout.Radial(Container.Elements,{ Origin = CFrame.new(0,5,0), Distance = 10, StartAngle = 0, Padding = math.rad(5), Axis = Vector3.new(0,1,0) }) Cinnamon.Layout.ApplyLayout(Container.Elements,Layout) Since layouts are just a Array of CFrames, you can also make your own custom layouts local Custom = function(Elements) local result = {} for i,Element in ipairs(Elements) do result[i] = CFrame.new(i,math.random(1,5),0) end return result end Cinnamon.Layout.ApplyLayout(Container.Elements,Custom(Container.Elements)) Animations Using the many animation options, Cinnamon allows developers to animate elements how ever they want. Cinnamon allows you to either animate using Tweens, Bezier curves, Springs or Oscillators local Tween = Cinnamon.Animation.Animate(Element,{ Type = "Tween" Property = "CFrame", Goal = CFrame.new(0,5,0), EasingStyle = "Sine", EasingDirection = "OutIn", Time = 1 }) Tween.Enabled = true Animations are considered objects as well, That means you only have to declare a Animation once to play it. This lets you dynamically change how the animation playslocal Frequency = 1 local Damping = 0.5 local Response = 0.2 local Spring = Cinnamon.Animation.Animate(Element,{ Type = "Spring", Property = "Offset", Goal = CFrame.new(0,5,0), Frequency = Frequency, Damping = Damping, Response = Response, Time = 1, }) Spring.Enabled = true task.wait() Cinnamon.Animation.SetGoal(Spring,CFrame.new(2,0,2)) We can also animate multiple elements, giving more creative options for our componentslocal ScreenGui = PlayerGui:WaitForChild("ScreenGui") local function BuildCarousel(Container : Cinnamon.UIContainer,ItemCount : number,Radius : number,Center : CFrame) local Carousel = Container:NewContainer(Container.UI,Center) for i = 1,ItemCount do local NewFrame = Instance.new("Frame",ScreenGui) NewFrame.Name = string.char(64 + i) NewFrame.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1,1) NewFrame.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.new(1,1,1) Carousel:Element({ UI = NewFrame, Offset = CFrame.new(0,0,0), Resolution = Vector2.new(800,600) }) end local A = Cinnamon.Layout.Radial(Carousel.Elements,{ Origin = Center, Distance = Radius, StartAngle = 0, Padding = math.rad(5), Axis = Vector3.new(0,1,0) }) local B = Cinnamon.Layout.Radial(Carousel.Elements,{ Origin = Center, Distance = Radius, StartAngle = 30, Padding = math.rad(5), Axis = Vector3.new(0,1,0) }) local C = Cinnamon.Layout.Radial(Carousel.Elements,{ Origin = Center, Distance = Radius, StartAngle = 30, Padding = math.rad(5), Axis = Vector3.new(0,1,0) }) Cinnamon.Layout.ApplyLayout(Carousel.Elements,A) return Carousel,{A,B,C} end local Container = Cinnamon.NewContainer(ScreenGui,CFrame.new(0,5,0)) local Carousel,KeyframeTable = BuildCarousel(Container,11,10.75,Container.Origin:ToWorldPosition(CFrame.new(0,0,-10))) local Forwards = Cinnamon.Animation.BatchAnimation("Tween",Carousel.Elements,{ Property = "CFrame", EasingStyle = "Quad", EasingDirection = "InOut" },{ Goal = KeyframeTable[2] }) local Backwards = Cinnamon.Animation.BatchAnimation("Tween",Carousel.Elements,{ Property = "CFrame", EasingStyle = "Quad", EasingDirection = "InOut" },{ Goal = KeyframeTable[3] }) Forwards:SetEnabled(true) task.wait(1) Cinnamon.Layout.ApplyLayout(Carousel.Elements,KeyframeTable[1]) Backwards:SetEnabled(true)

item.title: Layout
Screen Container
UI Container
item.description: Holds Elements and positions them in world position.Properties:Enabled : Boolean Enables/Disables child objects Debug : Boolean Adds/Removes itself and its child objects from the debug visualiser Origin : CFrame The point where its child objects are placed relative to Members: Elements : {Element} The Elements being stored Children : {UIContainer} The containers nested inside this container UI : ScreenGui The UI that stores your Elements Methods:NewContainer -> Containerfunction Container:NewContainer( UI : ScreenGui, Origin : CFrame ) : UIContainer creates a new child container Element -> Elementfunction Container:Element(Props : { UI : GuiObject, Offset : CFrame, Resolution : Vector2, Face : Enum.NormalId } ) : Element creates a new element Clear -> nilfunction Container:Clear() : nil Clears out and destroys child objects without destroying the container UDim2ToCFrame -> CFramefunction Container:UDim2ToCFrame( Position : UDim2, ViewPortSize : Vector2, DisplayDistance : number ) : CFrame Projects UDim2 to a position relative to the origin
